children.text: Chapter 1
athāto gṛhyakarmāṇy upadekṣyāmaḥ
children.translated_text: Now, then, we shall teach the domestic rites.

children.text: yajñopavītinācāntodakena kṛtyam
children.translated_text: The act is to be performed by one wearing the sacred thread, with water sipped for purification.

children.text: udagayane pūrvapakṣe puṇye 'hani prāg āvartanād ahnaḥ kālaṃ vidyāt yathādeśaṃ ca
children.translated_text: In the northern course of the sun, in the bright fortnight, on an auspicious day, he should know the time before the day's turning, and according to the locality.

children.text: sarvāṇy evānvāhāryavanti
children.translated_text: All of them indeed have an accompanying anvāhārya meal.

children.text: apavarge 'bhirūpabhojanaṃ yathāśakti
children.translated_text: At the completion there should be a suitable meal, according to one's ability.

children.text: brahmacārī vedam adhītyāntyāṃ samidham abhyādhāsyan jāyāyā vā pāṇiṃ jighṛksan anuguptā apa apāhṛtya prāgudakpravaṇaṃ deśaṃ samaṃ vā parisamuhyopalipya madhyataḥ prācīṃ lekhām ullikhyodīcīṃ ca saṃhatāṃ paścān madhye prācīs tisra ullikhyābhyukṣet
children.translated_text: A Vedic student, after studying the Veda, when he is about to put on the last fuel-stick, or when he is about to take his wife's hand, having brought water that has been protected, should clear a place sloping east or north, or level, sweep it all around and smear it; then in the middle he should draw an eastward line and a northward one joined to it, and afterwards three eastward lines in the middle, and sprinkle them.

children.text: laksaṇāvṛd eṣā sarvatra
children.translated_text: This is the rule of the characteristic layout everywhere.

children.text: bhūr bhuvaḥ svar ity abhimukham agniṃ praṇayanti
children.translated_text: With the words "<s>bhūr bhuvaḥ svar</s>," they bring the fire forward facing him.

children.text: prete vā gṛhapatau parameṣṭhikaraṇam
children.translated_text: Or, when the householder has died, there is the making of the parameṣṭhin rite.

children.text: tathātithinakṣatraparvasamavāye darśe vā paurṇamāse vā 'gnisamādhānaṃ kurvīta
children.translated_text: Likewise, when a guest, a lunar mansion, and a festival coincide, or at new moon or full moon, he should perform the placing of the fire.

children.text: vaiśyakulād vāmbarīṣād vāgnim āhṛtyābhyādadhyāt api vā bahuyājina evāgārād brāhmaṇasya vā rājanyasya vā vaiśyasya vā api vānyaṃ mathitvābhyādadhyāt puṇyas tv evānardhuko bhavatīti
children.translated_text: Having brought fire from a Vaiśya family, or from an āmbarīṣa, he should set it down; or else from the house of one who has performed many sacrifices, whether a Brāhmaṇa, a Rājanya, or a Vaiśya; or else, having kindled another by churning, he should set it down. But one that has no defect is auspicious, so they say.

children.text: yathā kāmayeta tathā kuryāt
children.translated_text: He should do it in whatever way he wishes.

children.text: sa yad evāntyāṃ samidham abhyādadhāti jāyāyā vā pāṇiṃ jighṛksan juhoti tam abhisaṃyacchet sa evāsya gṛhyo 'gnir bhavati
children.translated_text: That very fire on which he puts the last fuel-stick, or into which he offers when about to take his wife's hand, he should gather together; that becomes his domestic fire.

children.text: tena caivāsya prātarāhutir hutā bhavatīti sāyamāhutyupakrama evāta ūrdhvaṃ gṛhye 'gnau homo vidhīyate
children.translated_text: And by that his morning oblation has already been offered; from then onward, beginning with the evening oblation, offering in the domestic fire is prescribed.

children.text: purā prāduṣkaraṇavelāyāḥ sāyaṃprātar anuguptā apa āharet paricaraṇīyaḥ api vā sāyam api vā kumbhād vā maṇikād vā gṛhṇīyāt
children.translated_text: Before the time of bringing the fire into view, in the evening and morning he should bring protected water for tending it; or else in the evening, or from a pot or a small vessel, he may take it.

children.text: purā 'stamayād agniṃ prāduṣkṛtyāstamite sāyamāhutiṃ juhuyāt purodayāt prātaḥ prāduṣkṛtyodite 'nudite vā prātarāhutiṃ juhuyāt ||
children.translated_text: Before sunset, having made the fire visible, he should offer the evening oblation after the sun has set; before sunrise, having made it visible in the morning, he should offer the morning oblation when the sun has risen, or before it has risen.

children.text: yajñopavītam kurute sūtraṃ vastraṃ vāpi vā kuśarajjum eva
children.translated_text: He makes the sacred thread, whether of thread, cloth, or even a rope of kuśa grass.

children.text: dakṣiṇaṃ bāhum uddhṛtya śiro 'vadhāya savye 'ṃse pratiṣṭhāpayati dakṣiṇaṃ kakṣam anvavalambaṃ bhavaty evaṃ yajñopavītī bhavati savyaṃ bāhum uddhṛtya śiro 'vadhāya dakṣiṇe 'ṃse pratiṣṭhāpayati savyaṃ kakṣam anvavalambaṃ bhavaty evaṃ prācīnāvītī bhavati pitṛyajñe tv eva prācīnāvītī bhavati
children.translated_text: Lifting the right arm, placing it over the head, and setting it on the left shoulder, it hangs down under the right armpit; thus he becomes one wearing the sacred thread. Lifting the left arm, placing it over the head, and setting it on the right shoulder, it hangs down under the left armpit; thus he becomes one wearing the prācīnāvīta. But at the offering to the ancestors he is to be prācīnāvītin.

children.text: udag agner utsṛpya prakṣālya paṇī pādau copaviśya trir ācāmed dviḥ parimṛjīta
children.translated_text: Having moved north of the fire, washed the hands and feet, and sat down with the right knee bent, he should sip water three times and wipe twice.

children.text: pādāv abhyukṣya śiro 'bhyukṣet
children.translated_text: Having sprinkled the feet, he should sprinkle the head.

children.text: indriyāṇy adbhiḥ saṃspṛśet akṣiṇī nāsike karṇāv iti yad yan mīmāṃsyaṃ syāt tat tad adbhiḥ saṃspṛśet
children.translated_text: He should touch the sense organs with water, namely the two eyes, the two nostrils, and the two ears; whatever is to be ritually considered, that too he should touch with water.

children.text: tatraitad āhuḥ nopaspṛśed vrajan na tiṣṭhan na hasan na vilokayan nāpraṇataḥ nāṅgulībhiḥ nātīrthena na saśabdam nānavekṣitam na bāhyāṃsaḥ nāntarīyaikadeśasya kalpayitvottarīyatām noṣṇābhiḥ na saphenābhiḥ na ca sopānatkaḥ kvacit kāsaktikaḥ gale baddhaḥ caraṇau na prasārya ca
children.translated_text: On this point they say: he should not perform the water-touching while walking, nor while standing, nor while laughing, nor while looking about, nor without being bent forward, nor with the fingers, nor with an improper tīrtha of the hand, nor noisily, nor without looking at it, nor with the outer garment off the shoulder, nor after making part of the lower garment serve as an upper garment, nor with hot water, nor with foamy water; and nowhere should he do it wearing sandals, with something attached, with the neck bound, or with the feet stretched out.

children.text: antataḥ pratyupaspṛśya śucir bhavati
children.translated_text: Finally, having performed the repeated water-touching, he becomes pure.

children.text: hṛdayaspṛśas tv evāpa ācāmet ucchiṣṭo haivāto 'nyathā bhavatīti
children.translated_text: But he should sip only water that touches the heart; otherwise, from this point, he becomes as one who has eaten leavings, so they say.

children.text: atha pratyupasparśanāni suptvā bhuktvā kṣutvā snātvā pītvā viparidhāya ca rathyām ākramya śmaśānaṃ cācāntaḥ punar ācāmet ||
children.translated_text: Now the occasions for repeated water-touching are these: after sleeping, eating, sneezing, bathing, drinking, and changing one's garment, and after stepping onto a road or a cremation ground; although already purified by sipping, he should sip again.

children.text: agnim upasamādhāya parisamuhya dakṣiṇajānvakto dakṣiṇenāgnim adite 'numanyasvety udakāñjaliṃ prasiñcet anumate 'numanyasveti paścāt sarasvaty anumanyasvety uttarataḥ
children.translated_text: Having placed the fire properly and swept around it, with his right knee bent, to the south of the fire he should pour an añjali of water with "<s>Aditi</s>, give permission"; behind it with "<s>Anumati</s>, give permission"; and to the north with "<s>Sarasvatī</s>, give permission."

children.text: deva savitaḥ prasuveti pradakṣiṇam agniṃ paryukṣet sakṛd vā trir vā paryukṣaṇāntān vyatiharann abhiparyukṣan homīyam
children.translated_text: With "God <s>Savitṛ</s>, impel," he should sprinkle around the fire clockwise, once or three times; alternating the concluding sprinklings, sprinkling around, is the act connected with the oblation.

children.text: atha haviṣyasyānnasyāgnau juhuyāt kṛtasya vākṛtasya vākṛtaṃ cet prakṣālya juhuyāt prodakaṃ kṛtvātha yadi dadhi payo yavāgūṃ vā kaṃsena vā carusthālyā vā sruveṇa vaiva
children.translated_text: Then he should offer into the fire some food fit for oblation, whether cooked or uncooked. If it is uncooked, he should wash it and offer it after making it mixed with water; and if it is curds, milk, or barley-gruel, he may use a bronze vessel, a caru-pot, or a ladle.

children.text: agnaye svāheti pūrvāṃ tūṣṇīm uttarāṃ madhye cāparājitāyāṃ ca diśīti sāyam atha prātaḥ sūryāya svāheti pūrvāṃ tūṣṇīm evottarāṃ madhye caivāparājitāyāṃ caiva diśi samidham ādhāyānuparyukṣya tathaivodakāñjalīn prasiñced anv amaṃsthā iti mantraviśeṣaḥ
children.translated_text: In the evening, saying "To <s>Agni</s>, svāhā," he offers the first oblation, the later one silently, in the middle and in the unconquered direction; then in the morning, saying "To <s>Sūrya</s>, svāhā," he offers the first, and the later one silently, likewise in the middle and in the unconquered direction. Having placed on a fuel-stick and sprinkled around afterwards, he should pour the water añjalis in the same way; the special mantra is "you have consented."

children.text: pradakṣiṇam agnim parikramyāpāṃ śeṣaṃ ninīya pūrayitvā camasaṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yathārtham
children.translated_text: Having circumambulated the fire clockwise, poured away the remaining water, filled the cup, and set it in place, he proceeds according to the purpose.

children.text: evam ata ūrdhvaṃ gṛhye 'gnau juhuyād vā hāvayed vājīvitāvabhṛthāt
children.translated_text: Thus from then onward he should offer, or cause another to offer, in the domestic fire until the final bath at the end of life.

children.text: athāpy udāharanti kāmam gṛhye 'gnau patnī juhuyāt sāyamprātarhomau gṛhāḥ patnī gṛhya eṣo 'gnir bhavatīti
children.translated_text: And they also cite this: if she wishes, the wife may offer the evening and morning oblations in the domestic fire, for the wife is the household; this is the domestic fire, so they say.

children.text: niṣṭhite sāyamāśaprātarāśe bhūtam iti pravācayet ṛte bhagayā vācā śucir bhūtvā pratijapaty oṃ ity uccais tasmai namas tan mākhyā ity upāṃśu ||
children.translated_text: When the evening meal and morning meal are finished, he should have it announced, "It has become." Except with the speech of <s>Bhaga</s>, having become pure, he replies aloud, "oṃ"; and softly, "Homage to that; may that not fail me."

children.text: atha vāgyato balīn haret bhāṣetānnasaṃsiddhim atithibhiḥ kāmaṃ sambhāṣeta
children.translated_text: Then, keeping silence, he should carry out the bali offerings. He may speak to announce that the food is ready, and he may converse freely with guests.

children.text: atha haviṣyasyānnasyoddhṛtya haviṣyair vyañjanair upasicyāgnau juhuyāt tūṣṇīṃ pāṇinaiva prājāpatyā pūrvāhutir bhavati sauviṣṭakṛty uttarā
children.translated_text: Then, taking a portion from the sacrificial food and sprinkling it with sacrificial condiments, he should offer it into the fire silently, with the hand itself. The first oblation belongs to <s>Prajāpati</s>; the latter is for the good performance of the rite.

children.text: atha balīn hared bāhyato vāntar vā subhūmiṃ kṛtvā sakṛd apo ninīya caturdhā baliṃ nidadhyāt sakṛd antataḥ pariṣiñcet ekaikam vānunidhānam ubhayataḥ pariṣiñcet
children.translated_text: Then he should carry the bali offerings, either outside or inside. Having made a clean place, he should pour water once and place the bali in four parts. At the end he should sprinkle once; or, after placing each one, he should sprinkle on both sides.

children.text: sa yat prathamam nidadhāti sa pārthivo balir bhavaty atha yad dvitīyam sa vāyavyo yat tṛtīyam sa vaiśvadevo yac caturthaṃ sa prājāpatyaḥ
children.translated_text: The first that he places is the earthly bali. The second is connected with wind; the third belongs to all the gods; and the fourth belongs to <s>Prajāpati</s>.

children.text: athāparān balīn hared udadhānasya madhyamasya dvārasyābdaivataḥ prathamo balir bhavaty oṣadhivanaspatibhyo dvitīya ākāśāya tṛtīyaḥ
children.translated_text: Then he should carry other bali offerings. At the middle door of the water-vessel the first bali belongs to the water deity; the second is for herbs and trees; the third is for space.

children.text: athāparam baliṃ haret śayanam vādhivarcaṃ vā sa kāmāya vā balir bhavati manyave vā
children.translated_text: Then he should carry another bali, either to the bed or to the privy. That is a bali either for desire or for wrath.

children.text: atha sastūpaṃ sa rakṣojanebhyaḥ athaitad baliśeṣam adbhir abhyāsicyāvasalavi dakṣiṇā ninayet tat pitṛbhyo bhavati
children.translated_text: Then, with the mound, there is one for the beings of the <s>rakṣas</s> class. Then, after sprinkling this remainder of the bali with water, he should pour it down toward the south at the refuse-place; that belongs to the ancestors.

children.text: āsīna eva 'gnau juhuyāt āsīnaḥ pitṛbhyo dadyād yathopapādam itarān
children.translated_text: Seated, he should offer into the fire; seated, he should give to the ancestors; the others he gives as is appropriate.

children.text: svayaṃ tv evaitān yāvad vased balīn haret api vānyo brāhmaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: As long as he remains in residence, he himself should carry these bali offerings; or another <s>brāhmaṇa</s> may do so.

children.text: dampatī eva iti gṛhamedhivrataṃ strī ha sāyaṃ prātaḥ pumān iti
children.translated_text: The couple themselves do it: this is the observance of household ritual. It is said that the woman does it in the evening and the man in the morning.

children.text: sarvasya tv evānnasyaitān balīn haret pitryasya vā svastyayanasya vārthārthasya vā yajñād eva nivartate
children.translated_text: He should carry these bali offerings from every kind of food, or from food meant for the ancestors, or from food for a welfare rite, or from food intended for some purpose. It is from the sacrifice itself that it proceeds.

children.text: yady ekasmin kāle vrīhiyavau prakriyeyātam anyatarasya hṛtvā kṛtaṃ manyeta
children.translated_text: If rice and barley are prepared at the same time, having carried the bali of either one, he may consider the rite completed.

children.text: yady ekasmin kāle punaḥ punar annaṃ pacyeta sakṛd evaitad balitantraṃ kurvīta
children.translated_text: If food is cooked again and again at one time, he should perform this series of bali offerings only once.

children.text: yasya tv eṣām agrataḥ siddhyed niyuktam agnau kṛtvāgraṃ brāhmaṇāya dattvā bhuñjīta yasyo jaghanyaṃ bhuñjītaiveti
children.translated_text: But for whichever of these the appointed food is ready first, he should place the first portion in the fire, give the first portion to a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, and then eat. If it is ready last, he should simply eat it, according to the rule.

children.text: athāpy udāharanti
children.translated_text: Now they also cite a traditional saying:

children.text: etasyaiva baliharaṇasyānte kāmam prabruvīta bhavati haivāsya
children.translated_text: At the end of this very carrying of the bali offering, one may declare a wish; it indeed comes to pass for him.

children.text: svayaṃ tv evāsasyaṃ balim hared yavebhyo 'dhy ā vrīhibhyo vrīhibhyo 'dhy ā yavebhyaḥ sa tv āsasyo nāma balir bhavati
children.translated_text: He himself should carry the seasonal-crop bali: from the barleys up to the rice, and from the rice up to the barleys. This is called the seasonal-crop bali.

children.text: dīrghāyur haiva bhavati
children.translated_text: He indeed becomes long-lived.

children.text: viśrāṇite phalīkaraṇānām ācāmasyāpām iti baliṃ haret sa raudro bhavati sa raudro bhavati ||
children.translated_text: When the chaff has been distributed, he should carry a bali made of the rinsing water, saying, 'of the chaff, of the rinsing water.' That is the <s>Rudra</s> bali; that is the <s>Rudra</s> bali.

children.text: atha darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ
children.translated_text: Now, concerning the new-moon and full-moon rites.

children.text: saṃdhyāṃ paurṇamāsīm upavaset uttarām ity eke atha yad ahaś candramā na dṛśyeta tām amāvāsyām
children.translated_text: He should observe the fast on the evening of the full-moon day; some say on the following one. The day on which the moon is not seen is the new-moon day.

children.text: pakṣāntā upavastavyāḥ pakṣādayo 'bhiyaṣṭavyāḥ
children.translated_text: The fast-days are at the ends of the fortnights; the sacrificial performances are at the beginnings of the fortnights.

children.text: āmāvāsyena haviṣā pūrvapakṣam abhiyajate paurṇamāsenāparapakṣam
children.translated_text: With the new-moon oblation he sacrifices for the first fortnight; with the full-moon oblation, for the latter fortnight.

children.text: yaḥ paramo vikarṣaḥ suryacandramasoḥ sā paurṇamāsī yaḥ paramaḥ saṃkarṣaḥ sāmāvāsyā
children.translated_text: The point of greatest separation of sun and moon is the full moon; the point of greatest conjunction is the new moon.

children.text: yad ahas tv eva candramā na dṛśyeta tām amāvāsyāṃ kurvīta dṛśyamāne 'py ekadā gatādhvā bhavatīti
children.translated_text: But precisely on the day when the moon is not seen, he should perform the new-moon rite, even if, on occasion, the lunar path has already passed while the moon is visible.

children.text: trayaḥ pūrṇamāsīkalā bhavanti
children.translated_text: There are three divisions of the full-moon day.

children.text: saṃdhyā vāstamitoditā voccair vā
children.translated_text: It may be at twilight, or when the moon has risen after sunset, or when it is high.

children.text: atha yad ahaḥ pūrṇo bhavati pṛthag evaitasya jñānasyādhyāyo bhavati adhīyīta vā tadvidbhyo vā parvāgamayeta
children.translated_text: As for the day on which the moon is full, there is a separate chapter for knowledge of this. He should either study it, or learn the lunar observance from those who know it.

children.text: atha yad ahar upavasatho bhavati tad ahaḥ pūrvāhṇa eva prātarāhutiṃ hutvaitad agneḥ sthaṇḍilam gomayena samantaṃ paryupalimpati
children.translated_text: Then, on the day that is the fast-day, in the forenoon, after offering the morning oblation, he smears this altar-space of the fire all around with cow-dung.

children.text: athedhmān upakalpayate khādirān vā pālāśān vā khādirapālāśālābhe vibhītakatilvakabādhakanīvanimbarājavṛkṣaśalmalyaraludadhitthakovidāraślesmātakavarjam sarvavanaspatīnām idhmo yathārthaṃ syāt
children.translated_text: Then he prepares the fuel-sticks, either of khadira or palāśa. If khadira and palāśa are unavailable, fuel may be taken as needed from all forest trees, except vibhītaka, tilvaka, bādhaka, nīva, nimba, rājavṛkṣa, śalmali, aralu, dadhittha, kovidāra, and śleṣmātaka.

children.text: viśākhāni pratilūnaḥ kuśā barhiḥ upamūlalūnaḥ pitṛbhyaḥ teṣām alābhe śūkatṛṇaśaraśīryabalbajamutavanalaśuṇṭhavarjaṃ sarvatṛṇāṇi ājyaṃ sthālīpākīyān vrīhīn vā yavān vā carusthālīṃ mekṣaṇaṃ sruvam anuguptā apa iti yāni cānukalpam udāhariṣyāmaḥ na tad ahaḥ prasṛjyeta dūrād api gṛhān abhyeyāt anyatas tu dhanam krīṇīyān na vikrīṇīta abahuvādī syāt satyam vivadiṣet
children.translated_text: The branches are to be cut back; the kuśa grass for the barhis is to be cut near the root; for the ancestors likewise. If these are unavailable, all grasses may be used except śūkatṛṇa, śara, śīrya, balbaja, muta, vana, and laśuṇṭha. He prepares ghee, rice or barley for the cooked oblation, the cooking pot, the stirring spoon, the sruva ladle, and protected water, as well as whatever substitutes we shall state. On that day he should not go away; even from afar he should return home. He should buy wealth from another, but should not sell. He should be sparing of speech and should speak what is true.

children.text: athāparāhṇa evāplutyaupavasathikaṃ dampatī bhuñjīyātāṃ yad enayoḥ kāmyaṃ syāt sarpirmiśram syāt kuśalena ||
children.translated_text: Then, in the afternoon, after bathing, the husband and wife should eat the fast-day meal, whatever is desired by the two of them; it should be mixed with ghee, according to one skilled in the rite.

children.text: Chapter 2
puṇye nakṣatre dārān kurvīta lakṣaṇapraśastān kuśalena
children.translated_text: Under an auspicious lunar mansion, he should take a wife, one praised for her marks, according to one skilled in the rite.

children.text: tadalābhe piṇḍān vedyāḥ sītāyā hradād goṣṭhāccatuṣpathād ādevanād ādahanād iriṇāt sarvebhyaḥ sambhāryaṃ navamam samān kṛtalakṣaṇān pāṇāv ādhāya kumāryā upanāmayed ṛtam eva prathamam ṛtam nātyeti kaścanarta iyaṃ pṛthivī śritā sarvam idam asau bhūyād iti tasyā nāma gṛhītvaiṣām ekaṃ gṛhāṇe 'ti brūyāt
children.translated_text: If that is not available, earth-lumps are to be gathered from the altar, from a furrow, from a pond, from a cow-pen, from a crossroads, from a gambling-place, from a cremation ground, and from barren ground, a ninth from all of them together. Having made them equal and marked, he should place them in his hand and present them to the maiden, saying, 'Truth is first; no one transgresses truth. This earth is established in truth. May she become all this,' and, taking her name, he should say, 'Take one of these.'

children.text: pūrveṣāṃ caturṇāṃ gṛhṇantīm upayacchet sambhāryam api tv eke
children.translated_text: If she takes one of the first four, he should marry her; but some say that even the mixed one is acceptable.

children.text: klītakair yavair māṣair vāplutāṃ suhṛt surottamena saśarīrāṃ trir mūrdhany abhiṣiñcet kāma veda te nāma mado nāmāsīti samānayāmum iti patināma gṛhṇīyāt svāhākārāntābhir upastham uttarābhyāṃ plāvayet jñātikarmaitat
children.translated_text: With parched barley or with beans soaked in the finest liquor, a friend should sprinkle her, body and all, three times on the head, saying, "Desire knows your name; you are named intoxication; bring this man together," and he should pronounce the husband's name. With formulas ending in <s>svāhā</s>, he should bathe the lap with the two following verses. This is a rite concerning kinsfolk.

children.text: pāṇigrahaṇe purastāc chālāyā upalipte 'gnir upasamāhito bhavati
children.translated_text: At the taking of the hand, the fire is set down in front of the hall on a smeared place.

children.text: atha janyānām eko dhruvāṇām apāṃ kalaśaṃ pūrayitvā sahodakumbhaḥ prāvṛto vāgyato 'greṇāgniṃ parikramya dakṣiṇata udaṅmukho 'vatiṣṭhate prājanenānyaḥ
children.translated_text: Then one of the bridegroom's party, having filled a jar with firm water, carrying the water-pot, covered and silent, goes around the fire on its front side and stands to the south, facing north; another stands with the goad.

children.text: śamīpalāśamiśrāṃś ca lājāṃś caturañjalimātrāñ chūrpeṇo 'pasādayanti paścād agneḥ dṛṣatputraṃ ca
children.translated_text: They set down behind the fire, in a winnowing basket, fried grains mixed with leaves of <s>śamī</s> and <s>palāśa</s>, to the amount of four handfuls, and also the upper millstone.

children.text: atha yasyāḥ pāṇiṃ grahīṣyan bhavati saśiraskā sāplutā bhavati
children.translated_text: Then the woman whose hand he is about to take is veiled and bathed.

children.text: ahatena vasanena patiḥ paridadhyād yā akṛntann ity etaya rcā paridhatta dhatta vāsase 'ti ca
children.translated_text: The husband should clothe her with an unworn garment, with the verse beginning "Those who cut," and with "Put on, put on for clothing."

children.text: prāvṛtāṃ yajñopavītinīm abhyudānayan japet somo 'dadad gandharvāye 'ti
children.translated_text: As he leads her forward, covered and wearing the sacred thread, he should recite, "<s>Soma</s> gave her to the <s>Gandharva</s>."

children.text: paścād agneḥ saṃveṣṭitaṃ kaūam evaṃjātīyaṃ vānyat padā pravartayantīṃ vācayet pra me patiyānaḥ panthāḥ kalpatāṃ iti svayaṃ japed ajapantyāṃ prāsyā iti
children.translated_text: Behind the fire he should have her set in motion with her foot a mat rolled up, or another object of the same kind, and make her say, "May the path by which husbands are reached become ready for me." He himself should recite, "Let her come forth," if she does not recite.

children.text: barhiṣo 'ntaṃ kaṭāntaṃ prāpayet pūrve kaṭānte dakṣiṇataḥ pāṇigrāhasyo 'paviśati
children.translated_text: He should bring her to the edge of the sacrificial grass, to the edge of the mat. At the eastern edge of the mat she sits to the south of the bridegroom.

children.text: dakṣiṇena pāṇinā dakṣiṇam aṃsam anvārabdhāyāḥ ṣaḍ ājyāhutīr juhotyagnir etu prathama ityetatprabhṛtibhiḥ mahāvyāhṛtibhiś ca pṛthak samastābhiś caturthīm ||
children.translated_text: While she has laid her right hand on his right shoulder, he offers six oblations of ghee with the verses beginning "May <s>Agni</s> go first," and with the great vyāhṛtis, separately and collectively; the fourth is offered with the combined ones.

children.text: hutvo 'pottiṣṭhataḥ anupṛṣṭhaṃ patiḥ parikramya dakṣiṇata udañmukho 'vatiṣṭhate vadhvañjaliṃ gṛhītvā pūrvā mātā lājān ādāya bhrātā vā vadhūm ākrāmayed aśmānaṃ dakṣiṇena prapadena pāṇigrāho japatī 'mam aśmānam ārohe 'ti
children.translated_text: After offering, the two rise. The husband goes around behind her and stands to the south, facing north. Having taken the bride's joined hands, the mother first takes the fried grains, or the brother does; the bridegroom should make the bride step on the stone with the front of her right foot and recites, "Step onto this stone."

children.text: sakṛtsaṃgṛhītaṃ lājānām añjaliṃ bhrātā vadhvañjalāv āvapati taṃ so 'pastīrṇābhighāritam agnau juhoty avicchindaty añjalim iyaṃ nāry upabrūta iti aryamaṇaṃ nu devaṃ, pūṣaṇam ity uttarayoḥ
children.translated_text: The brother pours into the bride's joined hands a single gathered handful of the fried grains. She offers that into the fire after it has been underlaid and sprinkled with ghee, without separating her joined hands, with "This woman has spoken near"; for the two following offerings the formulas are "Now god <s>Aryaman</s>" and "<s>Pūṣan</s>."

children.text: hute patir yathetaṃ parivrajya pradakṣiṇam agniṃ pariṇayati mantravān vā brāhmaṇaḥ kanyalā pitṛbhya iti
children.translated_text: When the offering has been made, the husband, going around as before, leads her clockwise around the fire with the mantra, or a Brāhmaṇa does so, with "The maiden from her fathers."

children.text: pariṇītā tathaivāvatiṣṭḥate tathākrāmati tathā japati tathāvapati tathā juhoti evaṃ triḥ
children.translated_text: When she has been led around, she stands in just the same way, steps in just the same way, recites in just the same way, pours in just the same way, and offers in just the same way. Thus it is done three times.

children.text: śūrpeṇa śeṣam agnāv opya prāgudīcīm abhyutkrāmayanty ekam iṣa iti dakṣiṇena prakramya savyenānukrāmet mā savyena dakṣiṇam atikrāme 'ti brūyāt
children.translated_text: Having poured the remainder from the winnowing basket into the fire, they make her step out toward the northeast. Beginning with the right foot at "One for refreshment," she should follow with the left. He should say, "Do not pass beyond the right with the left."

children.text: īkṣakān pratimantrayeta suma￦galīr iyaṃ vadhūr iti
children.translated_text: He should address the onlookers with the verse, "This bride is auspicious."

children.text: apareṇāgnim audako 'nusaṃvrajya pāṇigrāham mūrdhadeśe 'vasiñcati tathe 'tarāṃ samañjantv ity etaya rcā
children.translated_text: The water-bearer, going along behind the fire, sprinkles the bridegroom on the region of the head, and likewise the other one, with the verse "May they unite."

children.text: avasiktāyāḥ savyena pāṇinā 'ñjalim upodgṛhya dakṣiṇena pāṇinā dakṣiṇaṃ pāṇiṃ sā￦guṣṭham uttānaṃ gṛhītvaitāḥ ṣaū pāṇigrahaṇīyā japati gṛbhṇāmi ta iti ||
children.translated_text: When she has been sprinkled, he raises her joined hands with his left hand, and with his right hand takes her right hand, including the thumb, palm upward; he recites these six hand-taking verses beginning "I take your hand."

children.text: samāptāsūdvahanti prāgudīcyāṃ diśi yad brāhmaṇakulam abhirūpam
children.translated_text: When these are completed, they lead her away in a northeastern direction to whatever Brāhmaṇa family is suitable.

children.text: tatrāgnir upasamāhito bhavati
children.translated_text: There the fire has been set down.

children.text: apareṇāgnim ānaḍuhaṃ rohitaṃ carma prāggrīvam uttaralomāstīrṇaṃ bhavati tasminn enāṃ vāgyatām upaveśayanti sā khalv āsta evānakṣatradarśanāt
children.translated_text: Behind the fire there is spread the red hide of a bull, with the neck toward the east and the hair upward. They seat her on it, silent. She indeed remains seated until the sighting of the stars.

children.text: prokte nakṣatre ṣaḍ ājyāhutīr juhoti lekhāsandhiṣv ity etatprabhṛtibhiḥ āhuter āhutes tu sampātaṃ mūrdhani vadhvā avanayet
children.translated_text: When the lunar mansion has been announced, he offers six oblations of ghee with the verses beginning "At the junctions of the lines." From each oblation he should let the remnant fall on the bride's head.

children.text: hutvo 'potthāyo 'paniṣkramya dhruvaṃ darśayati dhruvam asi dhruvāhaṃ patikule bhūyāsam amuṣyāsāv iti patināma gṛhṇīyād ātmanaś ca arundhatīṃ ca ruddhāham asmīty evam eva
children.translated_text: After offering, he rises, goes out, and shows her the pole-star, saying, "You are firm; may I be firm in my husband's family, I, so-and-so, of this man, so-and-so," pronouncing the husband's name and her own; and similarly <s>Arundhatī</s>, saying, "I am held fast."

children.text: athainām anumantrayate dhruvā dyaur ity etaya rcā
children.translated_text: Then he addresses her with the verse beginning "Firm is the sky."

children.text: anumantritā guruṃ gotreṇābhivādayate so 'syā vāgvisargaḥ
children.translated_text: After she has been addressed, she respectfully greets the elder by gotra; that is the release of her speech.

children.text: tāv ubhau tatprabhṛti trirātram akṣārālavaṇāśinau brahmacāriṇau bhūmau saha śayīyātām
children.translated_text: From then onward, for three nights, the two of them should eat food without pungent or salty seasoning, remain continent, and sleep together on the ground.

children.text: atrārghyam ity āhuḥ āgateṣv ity eke
children.translated_text: Here some say that the guest-offering is to be made; others say it is when they have arrived.

children.text: haviṣyam annaṃ prathamaṃ parijapitaṃ bhuñjīta śvo bhūte vā samaśanīyaṃ sthālīpākaṃ kurvīta tasya devatā agniḥ prajāpatir viśve devā anumatir iti
children.translated_text: First he should eat consecrated food fit for oblation; or, on the next day, he should prepare a common meal, a <s>sthālīpāka</s> (pot-cooked oblation). Its deities are <s>Agni</s>, <s>Prajāpati</s>, the <s>Viśve Devāḥ</s>, and <s>Anumati</s>.

children.text: uddhṛtya sthālīpākaṃ vyuhyaikadeśaṃ pāṇinābhimṛśed annapāśena maṇineti
children.translated_text: Having taken out the pot-cooked oblation and separated one portion, he should touch it with his hand with the formula "With the bond of food, with the jewel."

children.text: bhuktvo 'cchiṣṭaṃ vadhvai pradāya yathārtham
children.translated_text: After eating, he gives the leavings to the bride, as appropriate.

children.text: gaur dakṣiṇā ||
children.translated_text: A cow is the sacrificial fee.

children.text: yānam ārohantyāṃ sukiṃśukaṃ śalmalim ity etām ṛcaṃ japet
children.translated_text: When she mounts the vehicle, he should recite this verse beginning "The beautiful <s>kiṃśuka</s>, the <s>śalmali</s>."

children.text: adhvani catuṣpathān pratimantrayeta nadīś ca viṣamāṇi ca mahāvṛkṣān śmaśānaṃ ca mā vidan paripanthina iti
children.translated_text: On the road he should address crossroads, rivers, rough places, great trees, and a cremation ground with, "Let no waylayers find us."

children.text: akṣabha￦ge naddhavimokṣe yānaviparyāse 'nyāsu cāpatsu yam evāgniṃ haranti tam evo 'pasamādhāya vyāhṛtibhir hutvānyad dravyam āhṛtya ya ṛte cid abhiśriṣa ity ājyaśeṣenābhyañjet vāmadevyaṃ gītvārohet
children.translated_text: When an axle breaks, when a fastening comes loose, when a vehicle is overturned, and in other mishaps, they carry off that very fire; having set that same fire down nearby and offered with the vyāhṛtis, he should bring another substance and anoint himself with the remaining ghee with the verse "whatever, apart from us, has clung," sing the <s>Vāmadevya</s>, and mount again.

children.text: prāpteṣu vāmadevyam
children.translated_text: When they have arrived, the <s>Vāmadevya</s> is sung.

children.text: gṛhagatāṃ patiputraśīlasampannā brāhmaṇyo 'varopyānaḍuhe carmaṇy upaveśayantīha gāvaḥ prajāyadhvam iti tasyāḥ kumāram upastha ādadhyuḥ tasmai śakaloūān añjalāv āvapeyuḥ phalāni vā
children.translated_text: When she has come home, Brāhmaṇa women whose husbands and sons are living and whose conduct is good should make her get down and seat her on the hide of a bull, saying, "Here, cows, be fruitful." They should place a boy in her lap; into his joined hands they should pour small pieces, or fruits.

children.text: utthāpya kumāraṃ dhruvā ājyāhutīr juhoty aṣṭāv iha dhṛtir iti
children.translated_text: Having made the boy rise, he offers eight fixed ghee oblations, beginning with "Here is firmness."

children.text: samāptāsu samidham ādhāya yathāvayasaṃ gurūn gotreṇābhivadya yathārtham ||
children.translated_text: When these have been completed, having placed on a fuel-stick, he should salute the elders according to age and gotra, and then proceed according to the purpose.

children.text: athātaś caturthīkarma
children.translated_text: Now, then, the rite of the fourth day.

children.text: agnim upasamādhāya prāyaścittājyāhutīr juhoty agne prāyaścitta iti catuḥ agneḥ sthāne vāyucandrasūryāḥ samasya pañcamīṃ bahuvadūhya āhuter āhutes tu sampātam udapātre 'vanayet
children.translated_text: Having set the fire down nearby, he offers expiatory ghee oblations four times with "<s>Agni</s>, expiation"; in place of <s>Agni</s> come <s>Vāyu</s>, <s>Candra</s>, and <s>Sūrya</s>. Combining them, he should adapt the fifth oblation in the plural; from each oblation he should pour the mingled remainder into a water vessel.

children.text: tenaināṃ sakeśanakhām abhyajya hrāsayitvāplāvayanti
children.translated_text: With that they anoint her, including her hair and nails, have her hair and nails shortened, and bathe her.

children.text: ūrdhvaṃ trirātrāt sambhava ity eke yada rtumatī bhavaty uparataśoṇitā tadā sambhavakālaḥ
children.translated_text: Some say that union may take place after three nights. When she has menstruated and the bleeding has ceased, then is the time for union.

children.text: dakṣiṇena pāṇino 'pastham abhimṛśed viṣṇur yoniṃ kalpayatv ity etaya rcā garbhaṃ dhehi sinīvālīti ca samāpya rcau sambhavataḥ ||
children.translated_text: With his right hand he should touch her private part with this verse, "May <s>Viṣṇu</s> prepare the womb," and, after completing also the two verses "Place the embryo, <s>Sinīvālī</s>," they come together.

children.text: tṛtīyasya garbhamāsasyādisadeśe puṃsavanasya kālaḥ
children.translated_text: Near the beginning of the third month of pregnancy is the time for the <s>puṃsavana</s> rite.

children.text: prātaḥ saśiraskāplutodagagreṣu darbheṣu paścād agner udagagreṣu darbheṣu prācy upaviśati paścāt patir avasthāya dakṣiṇena pāṇinā dakṣiṇam aṃsam anvavamṛśyānantarhitaṃ nābhideśam abhimṛśet pumāṃsau mitrāvaruṇāvityetayarcā
children.translated_text: In the morning, after bathing with the head included, she sits facing east on darbha grass whose tips point north, behind the fire and on darbha grass whose tips point north. Standing behind her, the husband should touch her right shoulder with his right hand and then, with no intervening cloth, touch the region of her navel with the verse "Male are <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>."

children.text: atha yathārtham
children.translated_text: Then he proceeds according to the purpose.

children.text: athāparam
children.translated_text: Now another rite.

children.text: prāgudīcyāṃ diśi nyagrodhaśuṅgām ubhayataḥphalām asrāmām akṛmiparisṛptāṃ triḥsaptair yavair māṣair vā parikrīyotthāpayet yadyasi saumī somāya tvā rājñe parikrīṇāmi yady asi vāruṇī varuṇāya tvā rājñe parikrīṇāmi yady asi vasubhyo vasubhyas tvā parikrīṇāmi yadyasi rudrebhyo rudrebhyastvā parikrīṇāmi yady asy ādityebhya ādityebhyastvā parikrīṇāmi yady asi marudbhyo marudbhyas tvā parikrīṇāmi yadyasi viśvebhyo devebhyo viśvebhyas tvā devebhyaḥ parikrīṇāmi oṣadhayaḥ sumanaso bhūtvāsyāṃ vīryaṃ samādhatteyaṃ karma kariṣyatītyutthāpya tṛṇaiḥ paridhāyāhṛtya vaihāyasīṃ nidadhyāt
children.translated_text: In the north-eastern direction he should buy a banyan shoot that has fruit on both sides, is not broken, and has not been crawled over by worms, with thrice-seven barley grains or beans, and lift it up, saying: "If you are of <s>Soma</s>, I buy you for king <s>Soma</s>; if you are of <s>Varuṇa</s>, I buy you for king <s>Varuṇa</s>; if you belong to the <s>Vasus</s>, I buy you for the <s>Vasus</s>; if you belong to the <s>Rudras</s>, I buy you for the <s>Rudras</s>; if you belong to the <s>Ādityas</s>, I buy you for the <s>Ādityas</s>; if you belong to the <s>Maruts</s>, I buy you for the <s>Maruts</s>; if you belong to all the gods, I buy you for all the gods. The plants, becoming well-disposed, place vigor in this woman; she will perform this rite." Having lifted it up, he should wrap it in grass, bring it back, and set it in a place suspended above the ground.

children.text: dṛṣadaṃ prakṣālya brahmacārī vratavatī vā brahmabandhuḥ kumārī vāpratyāharantī pinaṣṭi
children.translated_text: Having washed a grinding stone, a brahmacārin, or a woman under a vow, or a Brāhmaṇa kinswoman, or a maiden, grinds it without turning back.

children.text: prātaḥ saśiraskāplutodagagreṣu darbheṣu paścād agner udagagreṣu darbheṣu prākśirāḥ saṃviśati paścāt patir avasthāya dakṣiṇasya pāṇer aṅguṣṭhenopakaniṣṭhikayā cāṅgulyābhisaṃgṛhya dakṣiṇe nāsikāsrotasyavanayet pumān agniḥ pumān indra ityetayarcā
children.translated_text: In the morning, after bathing with the head included, she lies down with her head to the east on darbha grass whose tips point north, behind the fire and on darbha grass whose tips point north. Standing behind her, the husband should take it with the thumb and ring finger of his right hand and pour it into her right nostril with the verse "Male is <s>Agni</s>, male is <s>Indra</s>."

children.text: atha yathārtham ||
children.translated_text: Then he proceeds according to the purpose.

children.text: atha sīmantakaraṇaṃ prathamagarbhe caturthe māsi ṣaṣṭhe 'ṣṭame vā
children.translated_text: Now the <s>sīmantakaraṇa</s> rite, for the first pregnancy, in the fourth month, or in the sixth or eighth.

children.text: prātaḥ saśiraskāplutodagagreṣu darbheṣu paścād agner udagagreṣu darbheṣu prācy upaviśati paścāt patir avasthāya yugmantam audumbaraṃ śalāṭugrathnam ābadhnāty ayam ūrjāvato vṛkṣa iti
children.translated_text: In the morning, after bathing with the head included, she sits facing east on darbha grass whose tips point north, behind the fire and on darbha grass whose tips point north. Standing behind her, the husband ties on her an even-numbered cluster of unripe fruits of the udumbara tree with the verse "This tree is full of nourishment."

children.text: atha sīmantam ūrdhvam unnayati bhūr iti darbhapiñjūlībhir eva prathamaṃ bhuvar iti dvitīyaṃ svar iti tṛtīyam
children.translated_text: Then he parts the hair upward: first with bunches of darbha grass, saying "bhūr"; a second time, saying "bhuvaḥ"; a third time, saying "svar."

children.text: atha vīratareṇa yenāditer ity etayarcā
children.translated_text: Then with something more vigorous, with the verse beginning "By which for <s>Aditi</s>."

children.text: atha pūrṇacāttreṇa rākām aham ityetayarcā triḥśvetayā ca śalalyā yās te rāke sumataya iti
children.translated_text: Then with a full vessel, three times with the verse "I invoke <s>Rākā</s>," and with a white porcupine quill with the verse "Those favorable thoughts of yours, <s>Rākā</s>."

children.text: kṛsaraḥ sthālīpāka uttaraghṛtas tam avekṣayet kiṃ paśyasītyuktvā prajām iti vācayet taṃ sā svayaṃ bhuñjīta vīrasūr jīvasūr jīvapatnīti brāhmaṇyo maṅgalyābhir vāgbhir upāsīran
children.translated_text: The dish cooked in a pot is kṛsara, with ghee poured on top. He should have her look at it and, after saying, "What do you see?" make her answer, "Offspring." She should eat it herself. Brāhmaṇa women should sit near her with auspicious words, saying, "May you bear heroes; may you bear living children; may your husband live."

children.text: atha soṣyantīhomaḥ
children.translated_text: Now the oblation for a woman about to give birth.

children.text: pratiṣṭhite vastau paristīryāgnim ājyāhutī juhoti yā tiraścīty etayarcā vipaścit puccham abharad iti ca
children.translated_text: When the dwelling has been established, having strewn around the fire, he offers ghee oblations with the verse "She who is transverse" and also with "The wise one carried the tail."

children.text: pumān ayaṃ janiṣyate 'sau nāmeti nāmadheyaṃ gṛhṇāti yat tad guhyam eva bhavati
children.translated_text: He states the secret name: "This male child will be born; his name is so-and-so." That indeed remains secret.

children.text: yadāsmai kumāraṃ jātam ācakṣīrann atha brūyāt kāṅkṣata nābhikṛntanena stanapratidhānena ceti
children.translated_text: When they announce to him that a son has been born, then he should say, "Wait before cutting the navel-cord and before putting him to the breast."

children.text: vrīhiyavau peṣayet tayaivāvṛtā yayā śuṅgām
children.translated_text: He should have rice and barley ground by the same procedure by which the shoot was ground.

children.text: dakṣiṇasya pāṇer aṅguṣṭhenopakaniṣṭhikayā cāṅgulyābhisaṃgṛhya kumārasya jihvāyāṃ nimārṣṭīyam ājñeti tathaiva medhājananaṃ sarpiḥ prāśayet jātarūpeṇa vādāya kumārasya mukhe juhoti medhāṃ te mitrāvaruṇāv ityetayarcā sadasaspatim adbhutam iti ca kṛntata nābhim iti brūyāt stanaṃ ca pratidhatteti
children.translated_text: Taking it with the thumb and ring finger of his right hand, he wipes it on the boy's tongue with "This is command." In the same way, for the production of intelligence, he should have him taste ghee; or, taking it with gold, he offers it into the boy's mouth with the verses "May <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s> grant you intelligence" and "The wondrous lord of the assembly." He should say, "Cut the navel-cord," and "Put him to the breast."

children.text: ata ūrdhvam asamālambhanam ā daśarātrāt ||
children.translated_text: After this, there is no touching of the child until ten nights have passed.

children.text: jananād yas tṛtīyo jyautsnas tasya tṛtīyāyāṃ prātaḥ saśiraskaṃ kumāram āplāvyāstamite vīte lohitimny añjalikṛtaḥ pito 'patiṣṭhate
children.translated_text: On the third moonlit night from the birth, in the morning of its third day, after bathing the boy together with his head, when the sun has set and the redness has passed, the father stands with hands joined.

children.text: atha mātā śucinā vasanena kumāram ācchādya dakṣiṇata udañcaṃ pitre prayacchaty udakśirasam anupṛṣṭhaṃ parikramyo 'ttarato 'vatiṣṭhate
children.translated_text: Then the mother, having covered the boy with a clean garment, hands him northward from the south to the father, with his head to the north; having gone around behind him, she stands to the north.

children.text: atha japati yat te susīma iti yathāyaṃ na pramīyeta putro janitryā adhīti
children.translated_text: Then he mutters the verse beginning, "May what is well bounded for you," according to the text, "May this son not die away from his mother who bore him."

children.text: udañcaṃ mātre pradāya yathārtham
children.translated_text: Having given him northward to the mother, he proceeds according to the purpose.

children.text: atha ye 'ta ūrdhvaṃ jyautsnāḥ prathamoddiṣṭa eva teṣu pito 'patiṣṭhate 'pām añjaliṃ pūrayitvābhimukhaś candramasam yad adaś candramasīti sakṛd yajuṣā dvis tūṣṇīm utsṛjya yathārtham
children.translated_text: Then, on the moonlit nights after this, among those first specified, the father stands, fills an añjali with water, faces the moon, releases it once with the yajus beginning "That moon yonder," and twice silently, and proceeds according to the purpose.

children.text: jananād daśarātre vyuṣṭe śatarātre saṃvatsare vā nāmadheyakaraṇam
children.translated_text: When ten nights from the birth have dawned, or after a hundred nights, or after a year, there is the giving of the name.

children.text: atha yas tat kariṣyan bhavati paścād agner udagagreṣu darbheṣu prā￦ upaviśati
children.translated_text: Then the one who is to perform that rite sits west of the fire on darbha grass with its tips to the north, facing east.

children.text: atha mātā śucinā vasanena kumāram ācchādya dakṣiṇata udañcaṃ kartre prayacchaty udakśirasam anupṛṣṭham parikramyo 'ttarata upaviśaty udagagreṣv eva darbheṣu
children.translated_text: Then the mother, having covered the boy with a clean garment, hands him northward from the south to the performer, with his head to the north; having gone around behind him, she sits to the north, on darbha grass with its tips likewise to the north.

children.text: atha juhoti prajāpataye tithaye nakṣatrāya devatāyā iti
children.translated_text: Then he offers oblations with the words, "To <s>Prajāpati</s>, to the lunar day, to the lunar mansion, to the deity."

children.text: tasya mukhyān prāṇān saṃmṛśan ko 'si katamo 'sītyetaṃ mantraṃ japati āhaspatyaṃ māsaṃ praviśāsāv ity ante ca mantrasya ghoṣavadādy antarantasthaṃ dīrghābhiniṣṭhānāntaṃ kṛtaṃ nāma dadhyāt etad ataddhitam ayug dāntaṃ strīṇām
children.translated_text: Touching his principal vital breaths, he mutters the mantra, "Who are you? Which one are you?" and, at the end of the mantra, "Enter the month of <s>Āhaspatya</s>, O so-and-so." He should give him a name made with an initial and final that are voiced, with a semivowel in the middle, ending in a long vowel or visarga. For women it should be without a taddhita suffix, of an odd number of syllables, and ending in ā.

children.text: mātre caiva prathamaṃ nāmadheyam ākhyāya yathārtham
children.translated_text: Having first told the name to the mother herself, he proceeds according to the purpose.

children.text: gaur dakṣiṇā
children.translated_text: A cow is the sacrificial fee.

children.text: kumārasya māsi māsi saṃvatsare sāṃvatsarikeṣu vā parvasv agnīndrau dyāvāpṛthivī viśvān devāṃś ca yajeta daivatam iṣṭvā tithiṃ nakṣatraṃ ca yajeta
children.translated_text: For the boy, month by month, after a year, or on yearly festival days, he should worship <s>Agni</s> and <s>Indra</s>, Heaven and Earth, and all the gods; after sacrificing to the deity, he should also worship the lunar day and the lunar mansion.

children.text: viproṣya jyeṣṭhasya putrasyo 'bhābhyāṃ pāṇibhyāṃ mūrdhānaṃ parigṛhya japed yadā vā pitā ma iti vidyād upetasya vā￦gād a￦gāt sambhavasīti paśūnāṃ tvā hi￦kāreṇābhijighrāmīty abhijighrya yathārtham
children.translated_text: After returning from a journey, having grasped the head of his eldest son with both hands, the father should mutter the verse beginning, "When my father," or, for one who has undergone initiation, "From limb to limb you are born." Saying, "With the hiṅ-call of the cattle I smell you," he smells him and proceeds according to the purpose.

children.text: evam evā 'vareṣām yathājyeṣṭhaṃ yathopalambhaṃ vā
children.translated_text: In just this way he should act toward the younger sons, according to seniority or as they are encountered.

children.text: striyās tūṣṇīṃ mūrdhany abhijighraṇaṃ mūrdhany abhijighraṇam ||
children.translated_text: In the case of a woman, he silently smells the head; he smells the head.

children.text: athātas tṛtīye varṣe cūḍākaraṇam
children.translated_text: Now, then, in the third year there is the cūḍākaraṇa, the first tonsure.

children.text: purastāc chālāyā upalipte 'gnir upasamāhito bhavati
children.translated_text: In front of the hall, on a smeared place, the fire has been set down.

children.text: tatrai 'tāny upak￭ptāni bhavanti
children.translated_text: There these implements have been prepared.

children.text: ekaviṃśatir darbhapiñjūlya uṣṇodakakaṃsa audumbaraḥ kṣura ādarśo vā kṣurapāṇir nāpita iti dakṣiṇataḥ ānaḍuho gomayaḥ kṛsaraḥ sthālīpāko vṛthāpakva ity uttarataḥ vrīhiyavais tilamāṣair iti pṛthak pātrāṇi pūrayitvā purastād upanidadhyuḥ
children.translated_text: On the south are twenty-one bundles of darbha grass, a bowl of hot water, a fig-wood razor, or a mirror, and a barber holding a razor. On the north are dung from a draught ox, kṛsara porridge, and a mess of cooked rice prepared without ritual purpose. In front, they should place separate vessels filled with rice, barley, sesame, and beans.

children.text: kṛsaro nāpitāya sarvabījāni ceti
children.translated_text: The kṛsara porridge and all the seeds are for the barber.

children.text: atha mātā śucinā vasanena kumāram ācchādya paścād agner udagagreṣu darbheṣu prācy upaviśati atha yas tat kariṣyan bhavati paścāt prā￦ avatiṣṭhate
children.translated_text: Then the mother, having covered the boy with a clean garment, sits west of the fire on darbha grass with its tips to the north, facing east. Then the one who is to perform the rite stands behind, facing east.

children.text: atha japaty āyam agāt savitā kṣureṇeti savitāraṃ manasā dhyāyan nāpitaṃ prekṣamāṇaḥ uṣṇena vāya udakenai 'dhīti vāyuṃ manasā dhyāyann uṣṇodakakaṃsaṃ prekṣamāṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, looking at the barber and meditating in his mind on <s>Savitṛ</s>, he mutters the verse beginning, "This <s>Savitṛ</s> has come with the razor." Looking at the bowl of hot water and meditating in his mind on <s>Vāyu</s>, he mutters, "With warm water, O <s>Vāyu</s>, moisten him."

children.text: dakṣiṇena pāṇināpa ādāya dakṣiṇāṃ kapuṣṇikām undaty āpa undantu jīvasa iti
children.translated_text: Taking water with his right hand, he moistens the right kapuṣṇikā lock with the words, "May the waters moisten you for life."

children.text: viṣṇor daṃṣṭro 'sīty audumbaraṃ kṣuraṃ prekṣata ādarśaṃ vā
children.translated_text: With the words, "You are the tooth of <s>Viṣṇu</s>," he looks at the fig-wood razor, or at the mirror.

children.text: oṣadhe trāyasvainam iti sapta darbhapiñjūlīr dakṣiṇāyāṃ kapuṣṇikāyām abhiśiro'grā nidadhāti
children.translated_text: With the words, "O herb, protect him," he places seven bundles of darbha on the right kapuṣṇikā lock, with their tips directed toward the head.

children.text: tā vāmena pāṇinā nigṛhya dakṣiṇena pāṇinaudumbaraṃ kṣuraṃ gṛhītvādarśaṃ vābhinidadhāti svadhite mainaṃ hiṃsīr iti
children.translated_text: Holding them down with his left hand and taking the fig-wood razor in his right hand, or applying the mirror, he says, "O axe, do not harm him."

children.text: yena pūṣā bṛhaspater iti triḥ prāñcaṃ prohaty apracchindan sakṛd yajuṣā dvis tūṣṇīm
children.translated_text: With the verse beginning, "With which <s>Pūṣan</s> shaved <s>Bṛhaspati</s>," he strokes forward three times without cutting: once with the yajus and twice silently.

children.text: athāyasena pracchidyānaḍuhe gomaye nidadhāti
children.translated_text: Then, cutting with an iron razor, he places the hair on the dung from a draught ox.

children.text: etayai 'vāvṛtā kapucchalam etayo 'ttarāṃ kapuṣṇikām undanaprabhṛti tv evābhinivartayet ubhābhyāṃ pāṇibhyāṃ mūrdhānaṃ parigṛhya japet tryāyuṣaṃ jamadagner iti etayaivāvṛtā striyāḥ tūṣṇīm mantreṇa tu homaḥ uda￦￦ agner utsṛpya kuśalīkārayanti yathāgotrakulakalpam ānaḍuhe gomaye keśān kṛtvāraṇyaṃ hṛtvā nikhananti stambe haike nidadhati yathārtham
children.translated_text: By this same procedure he should treat the kapucchala lock, and by this procedure the northern kapuṣṇikā lock, beginning again from the moistening. Taking the head with both hands, he should mutter the verse beginning, "Threefold life from <s>Jamadagni</s>." By this same procedure, for a girl, the rite is done silently, though the oblation is with the mantra. Having moved north of the fire, they pronounce him well. According to the custom of the lineage and family, after placing the hair on the dung from a draught ox, they carry it to the wilderness and bury it; some place it in a clump of grass. Then he proceeds according to the purpose.

children.text: gaur dakṣiṇā ||
children.translated_text: A cow is the sacrificial fee.

children.text: garbhāṣṭameṣu brāhmaṇam upanayet garbhaikādaśeṣu kṣatriyaṃ garbhadvādaśeṣu vaiśyam
children.translated_text: One should initiate a Brāhmaṇa in the eighth year from conception, a Kṣatriya in the eleventh from conception, and a Vaiśya in the twelfth from conception.

children.text: ā ṣoḍaśād varṣād brāhmaṇasyānatītaḥ kālo bhavaty ā dvāviṃśāt kṣatriyasyācaturviṃśād vaiśyasya ata ūrdhvaṃ patitasāvitrīkā bhavanti nainān upanayeyur nādhyāpayeyur na yājayeyur naibhir vivaheyuḥ
children.translated_text: Up to the sixteenth year the time has not passed for a Brāhmaṇa, up to the twenty-second for a Kṣatriya, and up to the twenty-fourth for a Vaiśya. After that they become fallen from the <s>Sāvitrī</s>; people should not initiate them, should not teach them, should not sacrifice for them, and should not marry with them.

children.text: yad ahar upaiṣyan māṇavako bhavati praga evainaṃ tad ahar bhojayanti kuśalīkārayanty āplāvayanty ala￦kurvanty ahatena vāsasācchādayanti kṣaumaśāṇakārpāsaurṇāny eṣāṃ vasanāni aiṇeyarauravājānyajināni muñjakāśatāmbalyo raśanāḥ pārṇabailvāśvatthā daṇḍāḥ kṣaumaṃ śāṇaṃ vā vasanaṃ brāhmaṇasya kārpāsaṃ kṣatriyasyāvikaṃ vaiśyasya etenaive 'tarāṇi dravyāṇi vyākhyātāni alābhe vā sarvāṇi sarveṣām
children.translated_text: On the day when the boy is to be initiated, that very morning they feed him, make him auspicious, bathe him, adorn him, and cover him with a new garment. Linen, hempen cloth, cotton, and wool are their garments; antelope, ruru-deer, and goat skins are the skins; muñja-grass, kāśa-grass, and tāmbalī are the girdles; and the staffs are of parṇa, bilva, and aśvattha wood. A Brāhmaṇa's garment is linen or hemp, a Kṣatriya's is cotton, and a Vaiśya's is woolen. By this same rule the other materials are explained. Or, if they are unavailable, all may be used for all.

children.text: purastāc chālāyā upalipte 'gnir upasamāhito bhavati
children.translated_text: In front of the hall, on a smeared place, the fire has been set down.

children.text: agne vratapata iti hutvā paścād agner udagagreṣu darbheṣu prā￦ ācāryo 'vatiṣṭhate antareṇāgnyācāryau māṇavako 'ñjalikṛto 'bhimukha ācāryam udagagreṣu darbheṣu tasya dakṣiṇato 'vasthāya mantravān brāhmaṇo 'pām añjaliṃ pūrayati upariṣṭāc cācāryasya
children.translated_text: Having offered with the formula, "O <s>Agni</s>, lord of vows," the teacher stands west of the fire, facing east, on darbha grass whose tips point north. Between the fire and the teacher, the boy stands with joined hands, facing the teacher, on darbha grass whose tips point north. Standing to his south, a Brāhmaṇa who knows the mantras fills an añjali with water, above the teacher.

children.text: prekṣamāṇo japaty āgantrā sam aganmahīti
children.translated_text: Looking at it, he mutters, "We have come together with the one who has come."

children.text: brahmacaryam āgām iti vācayati
children.translated_text: He makes him say, "I have entered <s>brahmacarya</s> (studentship)."

children.text: ko nāmāsīti nāmadheyaṃ pṛcchati tasyācāryaḥ
children.translated_text: The teacher asks his name, saying, "What is your name?"

children.text: abhivādanīyaṃ nāmadheyaṃ kalpayitvā devatāśrayaṃ vā nakṣatrāśrayaṃ vā gotrāśrayam apy eke utsṛjyāpām añjalim ācāryo dakṣiṇena pāṇinā dakṣiṇaṃ pāṇiṃ sā￦guṣṭhaṃ gṛhṇāti devasya te savituḥ prasave 'śvinor bāhubhyāṃ pūṣṇo hastābhyāṃ hastaṃ gṛhṇāmy asāv iti
children.translated_text: Having fashioned a name fit for respectful greeting, based either on a deity, on a lunar mansion, or on the gotra according to some, the teacher releases the añjali of water and with his right hand grasps the boy's right hand, including the thumb, saying, "At the impulse of god <s>Savitṛ</s>, with the arms of the <s>Aśvins</s>, with the hands of <s>Pūṣan</s>, I grasp your hand, O so-and-so."

children.text: athainaṃ pradakṣiṇam āvartayati sūryasyāvṛtam anvāvartasvāsāv iti
children.translated_text: Then he turns him around clockwise, saying, "Follow the course of the sun, O so-and-so."

children.text: dakṣiṇena pāṇinā dakṣiṇam aṃsam anvavaṃṛśyānantarhitāṃ nābhim abhimṛśet prāṇānāṃ granthir asīti utsṛpya nābhideśam ahura iti utsṛpya hṛdayadeśaṃ kṛśana iti
children.translated_text: With his right hand, after touching the right shoulder, he should touch the uncovered navel, saying, "You are the knot of the breaths." Moving upward to the region of the navel, he says, "Ahura"; moving upward to the region of the heart, he says, "Kṛśana."

children.text: dakṣiṇena pāṇinā dakṣiṇam aṃsam anvālabhya prajāpataye tvā paridadāmy asāv iti savyena savyaṃ devāya tvā savitre paridadāmy asāv iti
children.translated_text: With his right hand, touching the right shoulder, he says, "I hand you over to <s>Prajāpati</s>, O so-and-so." With his left hand, touching the left shoulder, he says, "I hand you over to god <s>Savitṛ</s>, O so-and-so."

children.text: athainaṃ saṃpreṣyati brahmacāry asy āsāv iti samidham ādhehy apo 'śāna karma kuru mā divā svāpsīr iti
children.translated_text: Then he instructs him, saying, "You are a brahmacārin, O so-and-so. Put on fuel-sticks. Drink water. Do the work. Do not sleep by day."

children.text: uda￦￦ agner utsṛpya prā￦ ācārya upaviśatyudagagreṣu darbheṣu pratya￦ māṇavako dakṣiṇajānvakto 'bhimukha ācāryam udagagreṣv eva darbheṣu
children.translated_text: Having moved north of the fire, the teacher sits facing east on darbha grass whose tips point north. The boy sits facing west, with his right knee bent, facing the teacher, on darbha grass likewise whose tips point north.

children.text: athainaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇaṃ muñjamekhalāṃ pariharan vācayatīyaṃ duruktāt paribādhamāne 'ty ṛtasya goptrīti ca
children.translated_text: Then, while putting the muñja-girdle around him three times clockwise, he makes him recite the verses beginning "This one, warding off evil speech" and "Protector of truth."

children.text: atho 'pasīdaty adhīhi bhoḥ sāvitrīṃ me bhavān anubravītviti tasmā anvāha paccho 'rdharcaśa ṛkśa iti mahāvyāhṛtīś ca vihṛtā oṃkārāntāḥ
children.translated_text: Then he sits near, saying, "Teach me, sir; may your honor recite the <s>Sāvitrī</s> to me." To him he recites it word by word, by half-verses, and by full verses, and also the great vyāhṛtis separately, ending with <s>oṃ</s>.

children.text: vārkṣaṃ cāsmai daṇḍaṃ prayacchan vācayati suśravaḥ suśravasaṃ mā kurviti
children.translated_text: And, handing him a wooden staff, he makes him say, "O well-famed one, make me well-famed."

children.text: atha bhaikṣaṃ carati mātaram evāgre dve cānye suhṛdau yāvatyo vā sannihitāḥ syuḥ
children.translated_text: Then he goes begging for alms, first from his mother, and from two other friends, or from as many as are present.

children.text: ācāryāya bhaikṣaṃ nivedayate
children.translated_text: He presents the alms to the teacher.

children.text: tiṣṭhaty ahaḥśeṣaṃ vāgyataḥ
children.translated_text: He remains standing for the rest of the day, keeping silence.

children.text: astamite samidham ādadhāty agnaye samidham ahārṣam iti
children.translated_text: When the sun has set, he puts on a fuel-stick, saying, "I have brought a fuel-stick for <s>Agni</s>."

children.text: trirātram akṣārālavaṇāśī bhavati tasyānte sāvitraś caruḥ
children.translated_text: For three nights he eats food without pungent substances and salt. At the end of that there is a caru offering to <s>Savitṛ</s>.

children.text: yathārtham
children.translated_text: According to the purpose.

children.text: gaur dakṣiṇā ||
children.translated_text: A cow is the sacrificial fee.
